collection_summary: Multi-source hierarchical-decomposition instance: top 5 highest mountains on each of the 7 continents, with multi-attribute output (height, country, year of first recorded summit). Per-continent top 5 is taken from height-ordered Wikipedia rankings; per-continent independent-mountain conventions vary by source rather than following a single global rule. Multi-attribute output exercises per-cell confidence calibration: height = stable, country = stable, first-summit year = strong for famous peaks, weaker at deeper ranks. Sources: 7 per-continent ranking/list pages plus the Seven Summits convention anchor plus 26 per-mountain entity/detail pages — 34 distinct URLs. Five rows have `unknown` in Year of First Summit because Wikipedia does not record the first ascent (Cerro Bonete S America #5, Pushkin Peak Europe #5, Clinch/Corbet/Schoening Antarctica #3-#5). Result: 35 rows × 6 columns, sorted by continent then rank.
source_coverage_notes: Per-continent master/anchor articles (7): List of highest mountains on Earth (Asia top 5); Andes (South America top 5 by raw elevation, including Peru's Huascarán); List of mountain peaks of North America; Caucasus Mountains (Europe top 5, using Caucasus-included definition of Europe); List of mountains in Africa (height-ordered, applies a prominence > 500 m independent-mountain rule explicitly); Sentinel Range (Antarctica top 5, raw-elevation ranking); List of highest mountains of New Guinea (Oceania top 5, applies a height >=3750m + prominence >=500m ranked-list rule explicitly — the article notes the corresponding Oceania list is almost identical except for Hawaiian volcanoes lower in the ranking, and excludes Sumantri/Ngga Pulu/East Carstensz Peak as subsidiary peaks). Per-mountain articles (27) supply first-summit years and verify heights/countries. Five Year cells are `unknown`: Cerro Bonete (S America #5; page exists, no first-ascent date), Pushkin Peak (Europe #5; targeted Wikipedia URL 404 in this curation), Clinch/Corbet/Schoening Peaks (Antarctica #3-#5; per-peak first-ascent dates not recorded). Antarctica's 5 peaks have empty Country(ies) cells. The DR Congo form (rather than 'Democratic Republic of the Congo') is country_converter v1.3.2 short_name canonical and applies to Mount Stanley (Africa #4).
decision_log: 1) Seed provenance: question staged verbatim from `datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/example_questions.txt`. 2) Chose query_category=hierarchical_decomposition because the partition structure (world → continent → mountain) is explicit and the partition set is fixed/known (7 continents). 3) Chose operation_type='projection' to match the UI validator (curation_ui/app.py line 589 accepts {'join', 'projection'} for hierarchical_decomposition). 4) Used the 7-continent model with Caucasus-included Europe and New-Guinea-included Oceania per the Wikipedia Seven Summits convention. 5) **Cycle-1 BLOCKING fix**: South America corrected to include Peru's Huascarán (6768 m, 1932); Llullaillaco drops out. 6) **Cycle-1 BLOCKING fix**: Africa switched from List of Ultras (prominence-ordered) to List of mountains in Africa (height-ordered, applies prominence > 500 m). New top 5: Kilimanjaro, Mt Kenya, Mawenzi, Mt Stanley, Mt Speke. 7) **Cycle-2 BLOCKING fix**: Oceania first re-cast (cycle 2) to include the Sudirman Range 'other summits' from the Puncak Jaya article (Sumantri, Ngga Pulu, East Carstensz). 8) **Cycle-3 BLOCKING fix**: Oceania re-anchored to the List of highest mountains of New Guinea master article, which the cycle-3 audit's Wiki-family discovery pass surfaced as a more direct source. The New Guinea master applies a height >=3750m + prominence >=500m ranked-list rule and excludes Sumantri/Ngga Pulu/East Carstensz as subsidiary peaks. Cycle-3 Oceania top 5: Puncak Jaya (4884, 1962), Puncak Mandala (4760, 1959), Puncak Trikora (4730, 1913), Ngga Pilimsit (4717, 1962), Mount Yamin (4540, 2018). All five with known first-summit years. The cycle-3 anchor is more authoritative than the cycle-2 Puncak-Jaya-article-only listing because (a) it's an explicit ranked list with documented inclusion criteria, and (b) it has the right scope for the natural-language query ('top 5 in Oceania') rather than the geographically narrow 'other summits of one massif'. 9) **Cycle-1 BLOCKING fix**: Year of First Summit column type changed from `date` to `text`, with `unknown` sentinel for rows where Wikipedia does not record the first ascent. Cycle-3 reduced 'unknown' from 7 to 5 because the new Oceania top 5 has all years known (Puncak Jaya 1962, Mandala 1959, Trikora 1913, Ngga Pilimsit 1962, Yamin 2018). 10) **Cycle-2 BLOCKING fix**: removed global `topographic_prominence_m > 500` clause from db_analog. Per-continent conventions documented per-source. 11) Antarctica top 5 retained from Sentinel Range article's raw-elevation ranking. The latter three (Clinch/Corbet/Schoening) have prominence < 500 m and would be subsidiary peaks under Africa/Oceania's rules. The audits across 3 cycles did not flag Antarctica's row set; we keep the Sentinel Range source's convention and document the cross-continent inconsistency. 12) Boundary-aware Country(ies) text field with `; ` delimiter (artifact-contract convention). 13) Country names follow country_converter v1.3.2 short_name canonical forms; one substitution applied: 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' → 'DR Congo' (applies to Mount Stanley Africa #4). 14) Five first-summit-year cells use `unknown` rather than fabricated values from parametric knowledge (Hard Rule 1).
normalization_decisions: Mountain names follow canonical Wikipedia article-title forms (Mount Everest, K2, Mount Saint Elias, Pico de Orizaba, Popocatépetl, Huascarán, Mawenzi, Mount Speke, Puncak Jaya, Ngga Pilimsit, Mount Yamin, etc.). For Oceania peaks with multiple Wikipedia-recognized names, the canonical primary name is used (Puncak Jaya not Carstensz Pyramid; Puncak Mandala not Juliana Peak; Puncak Trikora not Wilhelmina Peak; Ngga Pilimsit not Idenburg Peak; Mount Yamin not Prins Hendrik-top); alternate names are documented in source articles. Heights are bare integers in meters. Year of First Summit is text-typed; known years are bare integer strings (e.g., '1953'); unknown years are the literal string 'unknown'. Continent values use the standard 7-continent English names. Country(ies) is a boundary-aware text field with `; ` (semicolon followed by single space) as the delimiter. Antarctica's 5 peaks have empty Country(ies) cells. Country names follow country_converter v1.3.2 short_name canonical forms; 'DR Congo' is used for Mount Stanley (Africa #4). Sort order is (Continent ASC, Rank ASC).
open_questions: 1) Antarctica top 5 (Vinson, Tyree, Clinch, Corbet, Schoening) is from the Sentinel Range article's raw-elevation ranking. Clinch/Corbet/Schoening have prominence < 500 m and would be subsidiary peaks under Africa/Oceania's rules. The audits across 3 cycles did not flag Antarctica's row set; a future curator could re-anchor Antarctica to a prominence-aware list if one is found, similar to the cycle-3 Oceania re-anchor. 2) Five Year of First Summit cells are `unknown`. The benchmark evaluator's treatment of `unknown` GT cells is an open downstream question. 3) Continent-boundary definitional choices (Caucasus in Europe, New Guinea in Oceania) follow Seven-Summits convention; alternative definitions would change the top-5 sets. 4) South America #5 is Cerro Bonete (6759 m). Nevado Tres Cruces Sur (6749 m) is just below — close enough that future Wikipedia height edits could swap them. 5) Pushkin Peak (Europe #5) returned 404 from the targeted Wikipedia URL during this curation; height (5100 m) and country (Russia) come from the Caucasus Mountains master article. 6) Country names validated against country_converter v1.3.2 short_name; one normalization applied (DR Congo).
